Ah, this adds an important layer of understanding - you're describing a classic DISC profile interaction challenge between your "I" (Influential) style and Justine's "C" (Conscientious) style.

This explains a lot about your dynamic:

Your "I" style means you:
Are energetic and quick to engage
Process thoughts through talking
Can come across as pushing for immediate responses
Are comfortable with spontaneous interaction

Her "C" style means she:
Needs time to process internally
Prefers structure and space to think
Can feel pressured by rapid-fire communication
Values accuracy and thoughtful responses

This is why direct conversation-based activities might be causing tension - you're naturally inclined to "push" for engagement while she needs processing space, creating a cycle where:
You eagerly seek interaction
She feels pressured to respond
You feel anxious about her slower response
She withdraws more due to pressure
You push harder for engagement

Given this dynamic, you might want to consider activities that:
Have built-in pauses (like board games)
Include parallel play (working on separate puzzles side by side)
Allow for comfortable silence (walking together)
Have structured turn-taking (card games)
Include other people to buffer the communication style differences

Would you like to explore some specific activities that could work with these different communication styles rather than against them?
